item.title: How SpaceX Streamlined the Raptor Engine (17 minute read)
item.description: The differences between the versions of the Raptor rocket engine are stark. Many people initially didn't believe SpaceX when the company released a picture of the three generations of the design. The streamlining of the design also brought meaningful gains in performance - the Raptor 3 provides about 35% more thrust than the Raptor 1. This article looks at what specifically SpaceX changed that allowed it to take the Raptor from a tangle of wires and pipes into the svelte, streamlined engine it is today.

item.title: Helix 2.5: Zero-Shot 30-Home Generalization (14 minute read)
item.description: Helix 2.5 is an advanced neural network pretrained on Index, Figure's global-scale dataset of human behavior. It can tidy living rooms, fold towels, and make beds in homes it has never seen. The model is the first evidence that whole-body intelligence can be learned from human experience and transferred to new scenarios. Index is now generating roughly 35 minutes of new human experience every second - if Helix 2.5 is any guide, more data and compute should translate directly into more of the physical world learned before a robot ever enters a new home.

Trump has remained resolute that the nation needs to accelerate AI development and continue to build the data centers that are powering the AI boom.

item.description: Crusoe built one of the world's biggest AI supercomputers in Abilene, Texas. The company is now investing heavily in smaller data centers. It is manufacturing them in factories, loading them onto flatbed trucks, and deploying them wherever it can find available power. The company believes this is a faster and cheaper method than solely relying on large construction projects. Giant clusters with hundreds of thousands of chips are useful for training, but inference can be done with considerably smaller amounts of chips.

item.title: Mice with human brain cells offer a tool to study disease. Ethicists ask: What's next? (7 minute read)
item.description: Researchers have developed a technique for installing millions of human brain cells into mice. The scientists bred mice that were missing most of their cerebral cortexes and then replaced a large part of those missing mouse cells with lab-grown human brain cells. This resulted in mice with human neurons that could be altered to approximate human brain conditions. The technique could potentially create better scientific models for studying neurodegenerative disease.

item.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres (66 minute read)
item.description: Query optimizers continue to leave much to be desired despite an enormous body of research. A Postgres database should know everything about the stuff that lives in its tables, but the problem is enormously hard. What's not as hard is verifying whether a query plan an optimizer picks is good or not. Language models are particularly good at learning how to do tasks with easily verifiable outputs. A small, open-weights model can be post-trained via supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning to produce Postgres query plans that beat Postgres' default plans.

The MCP allows agents to analyze and answer questions about home activity, summarize camera footage across rooms, manage devices, and create smart home dashboards using everyday language. It contains safety protections, such as prohibiting sensitive actions like unlocking doors, but depending on the agent, using the MCP can result in unexpected or even undesired behavior.

item.title: SpaceX declares Starship ready for orbit, sets launch date next week (3 minute read)

The super heavy lift rocket will be carrying 26 of the larger V3 Starlink satellites into orbit 275 kilometers above Earth. The upper stage will seek to complete six orbits around Earth before completing its mission after about 10 hours. SpaceX will not attempt a return of the upper stage to the launch site in Texas on this mission, as it plans to gather more data about heat shield performance.

item.title: Is There Anything a Fruit Fly Brain Can't Do? (6 minute read)
item.description: Researchers at the Janelia Research Campus at the Howard Hughes Medical Institute in Virginia, in partnership with Google, recently published a new map of the adult male fruit fly's brain. The effort, which involved hundreds of scholars, resulted in a complete map of the fly's 166,000 neurons that can be trained to complete tasks like solving a Rubik's Cube or playing poker. Internet engineers and artists have made the model complete many seemingly impossible tasks for a fruit fly, like parallel parking a car, playing Doom, and trading cryptocurrencies.

The robot autonomously takes precautions when it detects a person at a distance, such as moving to avoid the person or standing still so the person can pass without getting closer. It can even choose to squat and assume a seated position if a person is getting too close. The robot will be available in early access within the first half of 2027 and become generally available by the end of the year.

item.title: Introducing the Agents API (5 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Agents API is now in public beta. The API brings the same harness and infrastructure that powers Codex to developers through a simple and flexible API. It allows developers to create useful agents with a powerful harness that manages context, uses tools efficiently, and coordinates subagents. The API provides infrastructure to keep agents running reliably for days, and environments where agents can work with files, run code, and save intermediate results.

item.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Possible Efforts to Build Biological Weapons (6 minute read)
item.description: Anthropic claims it has disrupted several plots to use its AI models to conduct research that could have helped develop biological weapons. The company says it still can't determine whether a query serves a legitimate or nefarious purpose, so it erred on the side of caution as the consequences of mistakes could be severe. Anthropic detected use from companies from blocked regions and parties that otherwise tried to obfuscate their purpose.

item.title: The lifecycle of a sharded Postgres query (23 minute read)
item.description: This post follows the journey of a PostgreSQL query through all of the layers of a complex sharded system. It aims to help readers understand what goes into making a large-scale sharded PostgreSQL deployment appear to be a single server even when spanning thousands of servers. A real database has hundreds of tables - the example in the post keeps the schema simple with two tables spread across four shards.

item.title: Router Power (14 minute read)
item.description: Centralized router platforms can offer customers better economics than local deployments. Outcomes pricing belongs to the infrastructure layer. The model layer could offer outcomes pricing, but it will have the same problems as the app layer. Router layer pricing is most politically aligned with customers, who just want to sell more compute and don't care which model is used.

It comes in two colors: Star White and Night Sky. More details on the device, as well as Apple's other recent releases, are available in the article.

item.title: Apple Takes on AI Wearables With Always-Listening Watch Features (4 minute read)
item.description: The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra models have new Audio Intelligence tools that use ambient listening to take high-level notes of wearers' conversations throughout the day. The devices will also have a Live Recap function that can show a transcription of what was said in a live conversation in the last 15 seconds and be able to listen to important sounds, such as a crying baby, doorbells, or sirens. These features will not create or store recordings, and Apple will not be able to access the raw audio. They will be available to test in English later this year. The improved Siri is being rolled out on watchOS 27 in beta on September 14.

item.title: Genome language models can design cancer vaccines (32 minute read)
item.description: Modern cancer-vaccine design involves identifying mutations, predicting presentation, predicting immunogenicity, ranking targets, and designing RNA. However, biology is complicated, and whether a target makes a good vaccine candidate depends on all kinds of information. This makes cancer vaccines an unusually direct test of whether AI models can take what it has learned from biology and apply that knowledge to design a medicine for one particular human being.

item.title: Scenarios for our Economic Future (12 minute read)
item.description: It is unknown yet whether AI will lead to unprecedented growth or widespread unemployment. Anthropic's Economics team built a model to understand how AI might affect jobs, growth, and unemployment in the US in the coming years. The model found that AI will lead to adverse impacts on wages and job prospects for knowledge workers in scenarios where growth is faster than anything in economic history, and in those scenarios, the challenge will be making sure wealth is broadly shared. The answer will depend on how AI affects all the tasks that make up the economy, the new tasks it creates, and how fast AI takes on this work.

item.title: Multimodal models need video. We froze time to give it to them (8 minute read)
item.description: PostHog's Replay Vision lets models view session recordings. This post looks at how PostHog built the tool and how it implemented a method for the model to actually see replays. It covers how PostHog built a custom rasterizer that runs hundreds of concurrent jobs across many pods. The custom rasterizer has so far rasterized more than 370 years of recordings into roughly 3.5 million videos since it was deployed in production in March.

item.title: Tailwind Labs is joining Shopify (3 minute read)
item.description: Tailwind is joining Shopify, one of the first companies operating at scale to see the potential of Tailwind CSS and start building with it. Shopify has invested in making sure Tailwind is actively maintained and will continue to provide a stable long-term home for the project. Nothing will change with Tailwind CSS or any of Tailwind's other open source projects, but the project will no longer try to grow its business. All existing customers will maintain access to their products, but Tailwind has closed signups for new customers.

item.title: Automattic's board forces CEO Matt Mullenweg into leave of absence (5 minute read)
item.description: Automattic's board has put founder and CEO Matt Mullenweg on a leave of absence against his will. The company's Chief Financial Officer, Mark Davies, had conspired with other board members to put Mullenweg on a paid leave of absence. Davies is now acting as interim CEO. Mullenweg remains the leader of the WordPress project, and the company's teams, priorities, and work will continue as planned. It is unclear why the board took this action. Mullenweg remains on the board of directors.
